title: Receptive fields, binocular interaction and functional architecture in the cat's visual cortex
authors: Hubel DH, Wiesel TN
summary: Characterized simple and complex cells and hierarchical receptive fields in visual cortex, inspiring hierarchical feature models from the Neocognitron to CNNs.

title: Machine Perception of Three-Dimensional Solids
authors: Roberts LG
summary: The 'blocks world' thesis: extracted edges from photographs and matched them to 3D polyhedral models, often cited as the start of computer vision.

title: Vision: A Computational Investigation into the Human Representation and Processing of Visual Information
authors: Marr D
summary: Framed vision as information processing across computational, algorithmic and implementation levels, with the primal sketch / 2.5D sketch / 3D model pipeline that shaped decades of research.

title: Determining Optical Flow
authors: Horn BKP, Schunck BG
summary: Global variational optical flow method combining brightness constancy with a smoothness prior; the foundation of dense flow estimation.

title: An Iterative Image Registration Technique with an Application to Stereo Vision
authors: Lucas BD, Kanade T
summary: Local least-squares, gradient-based image alignment (Lucas-Kanade), the basis of sparse optical flow and feature tracking.

title: Random Sample Consensus: A Paradigm for Model Fitting with Applications to Image Analysis and Automated Cartography
authors: Fischler MA, Bolles RC
summary: RANSAC: robust model fitting by hypothesize-and-verify on random minimal samples; ubiquitous in geometric vision.

title: A computer algorithm for reconstructing a scene from two projections
authors: Longuet-Higgins HC
summary: Introduced the essential matrix and the eight-point algorithm for two-view relative pose and structure recovery.

title: A Computational Approach to Edge Detection
authors: Canny J
summary: Derived an optimal edge detector with non-maximum suppression and hysteresis thresholding; still the standard edge detector.

title: Snakes: Active Contour Models
authors: Kass M, Witkin A, Terzopoulos D
summary: Energy-minimizing deformable contours for boundary extraction, launching the variational / active contour approach to segmentation.

title: A Combined Corner and Edge Detector
authors: Harris C, Stephens M
summary: The Harris corner detector based on the local structure tensor, a foundational interest-point detector for matching and tracking.

title: Eigenfaces for Recognition
authors: Turk M, Pentland A
summary: Face recognition by projecting images onto principal components ('eigenfaces'), a landmark of appearance-based recognition.

title: Normalized Cuts and Image Segmentation
authors: Shi J, Malik J
summary: Formulated segmentation as normalized graph partitioning solved via spectral relaxation; a cornerstone of grouping-based segmentation.

title: Rapid Object Detection using a Boosted Cascade of Simple Features
authors: Viola P, Jones M
summary: Real-time face detection using Haar-like features, integral images, AdaBoost and an attentional cascade; the first practical real-time detector.

title: Video Google: A Text Retrieval Approach to Object Matching in Videos
authors: Sivic J, Zisserman A
summary: Quantized local descriptors into 'visual words' for inverted-file retrieval, establishing the bag-of-visual-words paradigm.

title: Distinctive Image Features from Scale-Invariant Keypoints
authors: Lowe DG
summary: SIFT: scale-space keypoint detection with gradient-histogram descriptors invariant to scale and rotation; dominated matching, recognition and SfM for a decade.

title: Histograms of Oriented Gradients for Human Detection
authors: Dalal N, Triggs B
summary: HOG descriptors with a linear SVM for pedestrian detection; the dominant hand-crafted detection feature before deep learning.

title: SURF: Speeded Up Robust Features
authors: Bay H, Tuytelaars T, Van Gool L
summary: Fast scale- and rotation-invariant detector/descriptor using integral images and box-filter Hessian approximations.

title: Object Detection with Discriminatively Trained Part-Based Models
authors: Felzenszwalb PF, Girshick RB, McAllester D, Ramanan D
summary: Deformable Part Models: HOG-based root and part filters trained with latent SVM; state of the art on PASCAL VOC before CNNs.

title: Bundle Adjustment - A Modern Synthesis
authors: Triggs B, McLauchlan PF, Hartley RI, Fitzgibbon AW
venue: Vision Algorithms: Theory and Practice, LNCS 1883
summary: Comprehensive treatment of sparse nonlinear least-squares refinement of cameras and 3D points, the backbone of SfM and SLAM.

title: Multiple View Geometry in Computer Vision
authors: Hartley R, Zisserman A
summary: The standard reference on projective geometry, epipolar geometry, the fundamental matrix, and multi-view reconstruction.

title: Photo Tourism: Exploring Photo Collections in 3D
authors: Snavely N, Seitz SM, Szeliski R
summary: Large-scale structure from motion on unordered Internet photos (Bundler), enabling 3D browsing of tourist sites.

title: MonoSLAM: Real-Time Single Camera SLAM
authors: Davison AJ, Reid ID, Molton ND, Stasse O
summary: Real-time monocular simultaneous localization and mapping with an EKF over sparse features.

title: ORB-SLAM: A Versatile and Accurate Monocular SLAM System
authors: Mur-Artal R, Montiel JMM, Tardós JD
summary: Feature-based keyframe SLAM with ORB features, loop closing and bundle adjustment; a widely used SLAM baseline.

title: Structure-from-Motion Revisited
authors: Schönberger JL, Frahm JM
summary: Introduced COLMAP, a robust incremental SfM pipeline that became the default tool for camera pose estimation, including for NeRF data.

title: Neocognitron: A self-organizing neural network model for a mechanism of pattern recognition unaffected by shift in position
authors: Fukushima K
summary: Hierarchical network of alternating feature-extracting and pooling layers inspired by Hubel and Wiesel; the architectural precursor of CNNs.

title: Backpropagation Applied to Handwritten Zip Code Recognition
authors: LeCun Y, Boser B, Denker JS, Henderson D, Howard RE, Hubbard W, et al.
summary: Trained a convolutional network end-to-end with backpropagation on real zip-code digits, establishing the modern CNN.

title: Gradient-Based Learning Applied to Document Recognition
authors: LeCun Y, Bottou L, Bengio Y, Haffner P
summary: Presented LeNet-5 and the MNIST benchmark, and graph transformer networks for deployed check reading.

title: ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
authors: Krizhevsky A, Sutskever I, Hinton GE
summary: AlexNet: a GPU-trained deep CNN with ReLU and dropout that won ILSVRC-2012 by a wide margin, igniting the deep learning era.

title: Visualizing and Understanding Convolutional Networks
authors: Zeiler MD, Fergus R
summary: ZFNet: deconvolutional visualization of CNN features that guided architecture improvements and won ILSVRC-2013.

title: Very Deep Convolutional Networks for Large-Scale Image Recognition
authors: Simonyan K, Zisserman A
summary: VGG: showed depth with stacks of 3x3 convolutions improves accuracy; VGG features became a universal backbone.

title: Going Deeper with Convolutions
authors: Szegedy C, Liu W, Jia Y, Sermanet P, Reed S, Anguelov D, et al.
summary: GoogLeNet/Inception: multi-branch Inception modules with 1x1 bottlenecks; won ILSVRC-2014 with high efficiency.

title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
authors: He K, Zhang X, Ren S, Sun J
summary: ResNet: identity skip connections enabled training of 100+ layer networks; won ILSVRC-2015 and became the default backbone across deep learning.

title: Densely Connected Convolutional Networks
authors: Huang G, Liu Z, van der Maaten L, Weinberger KQ
summary: DenseNet: connects each layer to all subsequent layers for feature reuse and parameter efficiency.

title: MobileNets: Efficient Convolutional Neural Networks for Mobile Vision Applications
authors: Howard AG, Zhu M, Chen B, Kalenichenko D, Wang W, Weyand T, et al.
summary: Depthwise-separable convolutions with width/resolution multipliers for efficient on-device vision.

title: EfficientNet: Rethinking Model Scaling for Convolutional Neural Networks
authors: Tan M, Le QV
summary: Compound scaling of depth, width and resolution on a NAS-found base network, giving strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs.

title: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale
authors: Dosovitskiy A, Beyer L, Kolesnikov A, Weissenborn D, Zhai X, Unterthiner T, et al.
summary: Vision Transformer (ViT): a pure Transformer on image patches that matches or beats CNNs when pre-trained at scale, launching transformer-based vision.

title: Training data-efficient image transformers & distillation through attention
authors: Touvron H, Cord M, Douze M, Massa F, Sablayrolles A, Jégou H
summary: DeiT: trained ViTs competitively on ImageNet-1k alone using strong augmentation and a distillation token.

title: Swin Transformer: Hierarchical Vision Transformer using Shifted Windows
authors: Liu Z, Lin Y, Cao Y, Hu H, Wei Y, Zhang Z, et al.
summary: Hierarchical transformer backbone with shifted-window local attention, bringing ViTs to dense prediction; ICCV 2021 Marr Prize.

title: A ConvNet for the 2020s
authors: Liu Z, Mao H, Wu CY, Feichtenhofer C, Darrell T, Xie S
summary: ConvNeXt: modernized ResNets with transformer-era design choices, showing pure ConvNets can match Swin Transformers.

title: Rich Feature Hierarchies for Accurate Object Detection and Semantic Segmentation
authors: Girshick R, Donahue J, Darrell T, Malik J
summary: R-CNN: CNN features on region proposals with ImageNet pre-training and fine-tuning, nearly doubling PASCAL VOC mAP.

title: Fast R-CNN
authors: Girshick R
summary: Shared convolutional features with RoI pooling and a multi-task loss, making R-CNN training and inference much faster.

title: Faster R-CNN: Towards Real-Time Object Detection with Region Proposal Networks
authors: Ren S, He K, Girshick R, Sun J
summary: Region Proposal Network with anchors sharing features with the detector, yielding the canonical two-stage detector.

title: You Only Look Once: Unified, Real-Time Object Detection
authors: Redmon J, Divvala S, Girshick R, Farhadi A
summary: YOLO: single-network grid-based regression of boxes and classes, enabling real-time detection and spawning a long model family.

title: SSD: Single Shot MultiBox Detector
authors: Liu W, Anguelov D, Erhan D, Szegedy C, Reed S, Fu CY, Berg AC
summary: Single-stage detector predicting boxes from default anchors on multi-scale feature maps.

title: Feature Pyramid Networks for Object Detection
authors: Lin TY, Dollár P, Girshick R, He K, Hariharan B, Belongie S
summary: Top-down pathway with lateral connections building semantically strong multi-scale features; a standard detection neck.

title: Focal Loss for Dense Object Detection
authors: Lin TY, Goyal P, Girshick R, He K, Dollár P
summary: RetinaNet: focal loss down-weights easy negatives, letting one-stage detectors match two-stage accuracy.

title: End-to-End Object Detection with Transformers
authors: Carion N, Massa F, Synnaeve G, Usunier N, Kirillov A, Zagoruyko S
summary: DETR: set prediction with a transformer encoder-decoder and Hungarian matching, removing anchors and NMS.

title: Deformable DETR: Deformable Transformers for End-to-End Object Detection
authors: Zhu X, Su W, Lu L, Li B, Wang X, Dai J
summary: Sparse multi-scale deformable attention that speeds DETR convergence and improves small-object detection.

title: Grounding DINO: Marrying DINO with Grounded Pre-Training for Open-Set Object Detection
authors: Liu S, Zeng Z, Ren T, Li F, Zhang H, Yang J, et al.
summary: Open-vocabulary detector fusing language and vision in a DETR-style architecture, detecting arbitrary objects from text prompts.

title: Fully Convolutional Networks for Semantic Segmentation
authors: Long J, Shelhamer E, Darrell T
summary: Converted classification CNNs into fully convolutional networks with skip-connected upsampling for end-to-end pixelwise prediction.

title: U-Net: Convolutional Networks for Biomedical Image Segmentation
authors: Ronneberger O, Fischer P, Brox T
summary: Symmetric encoder-decoder with skip connections trained from few annotated images; dominant in medical imaging and later the standard diffusion denoiser.

title: Semantic Image Segmentation with Deep Convolutional Nets and Fully Connected CRFs
authors: Chen LC, Papandreou G, Kokkinos I, Murphy K, Yuille AL
summary: DeepLab: atrous (dilated) convolution plus a dense CRF for sharper semantic segmentation.

title: Mask R-CNN
authors: He K, Gkioxari G, Dollár P, Girshick R
summary: Extended Faster R-CNN with a mask branch and RoIAlign for instance segmentation; ICCV 2017 Marr Prize.

title: Masked-attention Mask Transformer for Universal Image Segmentation
authors: Cheng B, Misra I, Schwing AG, Kirillov A, Girdhar R
summary: Mask2Former: a single mask-classification transformer architecture for semantic, instance and panoptic segmentation.

title: Segment Anything
authors: Kirillov A, Mintun E, Ravi N, Mao H, Rolland C, Gustafson L, et al.
summary: SAM: a promptable segmentation foundation model trained on the SA-1B dataset of over 1 billion masks, with strong zero-shot transfer.

title: SAM 2: Segment Anything in Images and Videos
authors: Ravi N, Gabeur V, Hu YT, Hu R, Ryali C, Ma T, et al.
summary: Extended SAM to video with a streaming memory architecture for promptable video object segmentation, trained on the SA-V dataset.

title: Discriminative Unsupervised Feature Learning with Convolutional Neural Networks
authors: Dosovitskiy A, Springenberg JT, Riedmiller M, Brox T
summary: Exemplar CNN: treats each image and its augmentations as a surrogate class, an early instance-discrimination approach to self-supervision.

title: Unsupervised Feature Learning via Non-Parametric Instance Discrimination
authors: Wu Z, Xiong Y, Yu SX, Lin D
summary: Instance discrimination with a memory bank and NCE loss, a direct precursor to MoCo and SimCLR.

title: Momentum Contrast for Unsupervised Visual Representation Learning
authors: He K, Fan H, Wu Y, Xie S, Girshick R
summary: MoCo: contrastive learning with a queue of negatives and a momentum encoder, rivaling supervised pre-training for transfer.

title: A Simple Framework for Contrastive Learning of Visual Representations
authors: Chen T, Kornblith S, Norouzi M, Hinton G
summary: SimCLR: in-batch contrastive learning with strong augmentation and a projection head, showing the key ingredients of contrastive SSL.

title: Bootstrap Your Own Latent: A New Approach to Self-Supervised Learning
authors: Grill JB, Strub F, Altché F, Tallec C, Richemond PH, Buchatskaya E, et al.
summary: BYOL: self-supervised learning without negatives via an online network predicting a momentum target network.

title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision
authors: Radford A, Kim JW, Hallacy C, Ramesh A, Goh G, Agarwal S, et al.
summary: CLIP: contrastive image-text pre-training on 400M web pairs, enabling zero-shot classification and becoming the core vision-language component of generative models.

title: Scaling Up Visual and Vision-Language Representation Learning With Noisy Text Supervision
authors: Jia C, Yang Y, Xia Y, Chen YT, Parekh Z, Pham H, et al.
summary: ALIGN: dual-encoder contrastive training on over a billion noisy alt-text pairs, showing scale overcomes noise.

title: Emerging Properties in Self-Supervised Vision Transformers
authors: Caron M, Touvron H, Misra I, Jégou H, Mairal J, Bojanowski P, Joulin A
summary: DINO: self-distillation with no labels for ViTs, revealing emergent object segmentation in attention maps and strong k-NN features.

title: Masked Autoencoders Are Scalable Vision Learners
authors: He K, Chen X, Xie S, Li Y, Dollár P, Girshick R
summary: MAE: reconstructing pixels from heavily (75%) masked patches with an asymmetric encoder-decoder; simple, scalable ViT pre-training.

title: DINOv2: Learning Robust Visual Features without Supervision
authors: Oquab M, Darcet T, Moutakanni T, Vo H, Szafraniec M, Khalidov V, et al.
summary: Scaled discriminative self-supervised ViT training on a curated 142M-image dataset, producing general-purpose frozen features.

title: Depth Anything: Unleashing the Power of Large-Scale Unlabeled Data
authors: Yang L, Kang B, Huang Z, Xu X, Feng J, Zhao H
summary: Monocular depth foundation model trained with pseudo-labels on ~62M unlabeled images on a DINOv2 encoder, with strong zero-shot generalization.

title: DINOv3
authors: Siméoni O, Vo HV, Seitzer M, Baldassarre F, Oquab M, Jose C, et al.
summary: Scaled DINO-style self-supervised training to a 7B-parameter ViT on 1.7B images, with Gram anchoring to keep dense features high quality.

title: PointNet: Deep Learning on Point Sets for 3D Classification and Segmentation
authors: Qi CR, Su H, Mo K, Guibas LJ
summary: Permutation-invariant network operating directly on raw point clouds via shared MLPs and symmetric pooling.

title: NeRF: Representing Scenes as Neural Radiance Fields for View Synthesis
authors: Mildenhall B, Srinivasan PP, Tancik M, Barron JT, Ramamoorthi R, Ng R
summary: Represented a scene as an MLP mapping position and view direction to density and color, rendered by differentiable volume rendering for photorealistic novel view synthesis.

title: DreamFusion: Text-to-3D using 2D Diffusion
authors: Poole B, Jain A, Barron JT, Mildenhall B
summary: Score distillation sampling optimizes a NeRF using a pretrained 2D text-to-image diffusion model, enabling text-to-3D without 3D data.

title: 3D Gaussian Splatting for Real-Time Radiance Field Rendering
authors: Kerbl B, Kopanas G, Leimkühler T, Drettakis G
summary: Represents scenes as optimized anisotropic 3D Gaussians rasterized differentiably, achieving NeRF-quality view synthesis at real-time frame rates.

title: DUSt3R: Geometric 3D Vision Made Easy
authors: Wang S, Leroy V, Cabon Y, Chidlovskii B, Revaud J
summary: Regresses dense pointmaps from uncalibrated image pairs with a transformer, unifying calibration, pose and reconstruction without classical SfM.

title: VGGT: Visual Geometry Grounded Transformer
authors: Wang J, Chen M, Karaev N, Vedaldi A, Rupprecht C, Novotny D
summary: Feed-forward transformer that predicts cameras, depth, pointmaps and tracks from many views in one pass; CVPR 2025 best paper.

title: Two-Stream Convolutional Networks for Action Recognition in Videos
authors: Simonyan K, Zisserman A
summary: Separate spatial (RGB) and temporal (optical flow) CNN streams fused for action recognition.

title: Learning Spatiotemporal Features with 3D Convolutional Networks
authors: Tran D, Bourdev L, Fergus R, Torresani L, Paluri M
summary: C3D: 3x3x3 convolutions over space-time learn generic video features.

title: FlowNet: Learning Optical Flow with Convolutional Networks
authors: Dosovitskiy A, Fischer P, Ilg E, Häusser P, Hazırbaş C, Golkov V, et al.
summary: First end-to-end CNN for optical flow estimation, trained on synthetic Flying Chairs data.

title: Quo Vadis, Action Recognition? A New Model and the Kinetics Dataset
authors: Carreira J, Zisserman A
summary: I3D: inflated 2D ImageNet filters into 3D two-stream ConvNets and showed Kinetics pre-training transfers strongly.

title: SlowFast Networks for Video Recognition
authors: Feichtenhofer C, Fan H, Malik J, He K
summary: Two pathways at low and high frame rates capturing semantics and motion, a strong video recognition backbone.

title: RAFT: Recurrent All-Pairs Field Transforms for Optical Flow
authors: Teed Z, Deng J
summary: All-pairs correlation volumes with recurrent iterative updates; ECCV 2020 best paper and a new optical flow standard.

title: Is Space-Time Attention All You Need for Video Understanding?
authors: Bertasius G, Wang H, Torresani L
summary: TimeSformer: convolution-free video transformer with divided space-time attention.

title: Video Diffusion Models
authors: Ho J, Salimans T, Gritsenko A, Chan W, Norouzi M, Fleet DJ
summary: Extended diffusion models to video with a space-time factorized 3D U-Net and joint image-video training.

title: Video generation models as world simulators
authors: Brooks T, Peebles B, Holmes C, DePue W, Guo Y, Jing L, et al.
summary: Sora: a diffusion transformer over spacetime latent patches generating minute-long, high-fidelity videos, marking a leap in video generation.

title: Image Style Transfer Using Convolutional Neural Networks
authors: Gatys LA, Ecker AS, Bethge M
summary: Neural style transfer: optimizes an image to match CNN content features and Gram-matrix style statistics.

title: Unsupervised Representation Learning with Deep Convolutional Generative Adversarial Networks
authors: Radford A, Metz L, Chintala S
summary: DCGAN: architectural guidelines for stable convolutional GANs and meaningful latent arithmetic.

title: Image-to-Image Translation with Conditional Adversarial Networks
authors: Isola P, Zhu JY, Zhou T, Efros AA
summary: pix2pix: conditional GAN with U-Net generator and PatchGAN discriminator for paired image translation.

title: Unpaired Image-to-Image Translation using Cycle-Consistent Adversarial Networks
authors: Zhu JY, Park T, Isola P, Efros AA
summary: CycleGAN: cycle-consistency loss enabling translation between domains without paired data.

title: Neural Discrete Representation Learning
authors: van den Oord A, Vinyals O, Kavukcuoglu K
summary: VQ-VAE: discrete latent codes learned by vector quantization, a basis for tokenized image generation.

title: A Style-Based Generator Architecture for Generative Adversarial Networks
authors: Karras T, Laine S, Aila T
summary: StyleGAN: mapping network and AdaIN style modulation giving disentangled control and state-of-the-art photorealism; introduced FFHQ.

title: Taming Transformers for High-Resolution Image Synthesis
authors: Esser P, Rombach R, Ommer B
summary: VQGAN: adversarially trained perceptual codebook plus an autoregressive transformer prior for high-resolution synthesis.

title: Zero-Shot Text-to-Image Generation
authors: Ramesh A, Pavlov M, Goh G, Gray S, Voss C, Radford A, et al.
summary: DALL-E: a 12B-parameter autoregressive transformer over text and discrete image tokens, demonstrating compositional zero-shot text-to-image generation.

title: Diffusion Models Beat GANs on Image Synthesis
authors: Dhariwal P, Nichol A
summary: Improved diffusion architectures and classifier guidance surpassed BigGAN on ImageNet sample quality.

title: GLIDE: Towards Photorealistic Image Generation and Editing with Text-Guided Diffusion Models
authors: Nichol A, Dhariwal P, Ramesh A, Shyam P, Mishkin P, McGrew B, et al.
summary: Text-conditional diffusion comparing CLIP guidance with classifier-free guidance, with inpainting-based editing.

title: Hierarchical Text-Conditional Image Generation with CLIP Latents
authors: Ramesh A, Dhariwal P, Nichol A, Chu C, Chen M
summary: DALL-E 2 (unCLIP): a prior maps text to CLIP image embeddings and a diffusion decoder renders them.

title: Photorealistic Text-to-Image Diffusion Models with Deep Language Understanding
authors: Saharia C, Chan W, Saxena S, Li L, Whang J, Denton E, et al.
summary: Imagen: cascaded pixel diffusion conditioned on a frozen T5 text encoder, showing language-model scale matters most.

title: High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models
authors: Rombach R, Blattmann A, Lorenz D, Esser P, Ommer B
summary: Latent diffusion in a pretrained autoencoder's latent space with cross-attention conditioning; the basis of open-source Stable Diffusion.

title: Adding Conditional Control to Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
authors: Zhang L, Rao A, Agrawala M
summary: ControlNet: a trainable copy of the diffusion encoder connected via zero-initialized convolutions adds spatial conditions such as edges, depth and pose.

title: Scalable Diffusion Models with Transformers
authors: Peebles W, Xie S
summary: DiT: replaces the U-Net with a transformer over latent patches, showing diffusion quality scales cleanly with compute; basis of Sora and SD3.

title: Scaling Rectified Flow Transformers for High-Resolution Image Synthesis
authors: Esser P, Kulal S, Blattmann A, Entezari R, Müller J, Saini H, et al.
summary: Stable Diffusion 3: rectified-flow training with a multimodal diffusion transformer (MM-DiT), scaling to 8B parameters.

title: Visual Autoregressive Modeling: Scalable Image Generation via Next-Scale Prediction
authors: Tian K, Jiang Y, Yuan Z, Peng B, Wang L
summary: VAR: coarse-to-fine next-scale autoregressive prediction that outperforms diffusion transformers on ImageNet; NeurIPS 2024 best paper.

title: Learning Generative Visual Models from Few Training Examples: An Incremental Bayesian Approach Tested on 101 Object Categories
authors: Fei-Fei L, Fergus R, Perona P
venue: CVPR Workshop on Generative-Model Based Vision 2004
summary: Introduced Caltech-101, an early multi-category object recognition benchmark.

title: ImageNet: A Large-Scale Hierarchical Image Database
authors: Deng J, Dong W, Socher R, Li LJ, Li K, Fei-Fei L
summary: Millions of images organized by WordNet synsets and crowd-labeled; its ILSVRC subset catalyzed the deep learning revolution.

title: The Pascal Visual Object Classes (VOC) Challenge
authors: Everingham M, Van Gool L, Williams CKI, Winn J, Zisserman A
summary: Annual benchmark (2005-2012) for classification, detection and segmentation that standardized mAP evaluation.

title: Are we ready for Autonomous Driving? The KITTI Vision Benchmark Suite
authors: Geiger A, Lenz P, Urtasun R
summary: Driving benchmark for stereo, optical flow, visual odometry and 3D detection from a sensor-equipped car.

title: UCF101: A Dataset of 101 Human Actions Classes From Videos in The Wild
authors: Soomro K, Zamir AR, Shah M
summary: 13K YouTube clips across 101 actions; a standard action recognition benchmark of the early deep era.

title: Microsoft COCO: Common Objects in Context
authors: Lin TY, Maire M, Belongie S, Hays J, Perona P, Ramanan D, et al.
summary: Large-scale dataset with instance segmentation of 80 categories in context plus captions; the primary detection and segmentation benchmark.

title: ImageNet Large Scale Visual Recognition Challenge
authors: Russakovsky O, Deng J, Su H, Krause J, Satheesh S, Ma S, et al.
summary: Describes the ILSVRC benchmark (2010-2017) and its role in tracking progress from hand-crafted features to deep CNNs.

title: The Cityscapes Dataset for Semantic Urban Scene Understanding
authors: Cordts M, Omran M, Ramos S, Rehfeld T, Enzweiler M, Benenson R, et al.
summary: High-quality pixel-level annotations of urban street scenes from 50 cities; the standard driving segmentation benchmark.

title: The Kinetics Human Action Video Dataset
authors: Kay W, Carreira J, Simonyan K, Zhang B, Hillier C, Vijayanarasimhan S, et al.
summary: Large-scale YouTube action dataset (400 classes, later 600/700) that became the ImageNet of video recognition.

title: LAION-5B: An open large-scale dataset for training next generation image-text models
authors: Schuhmann C, Beaumont R, Vencu R, Gordon C, Wightman R, Cherti M, et al.
summary: 5.85B CLIP-filtered web image-text pairs released openly, enabling open CLIP replications and Stable Diffusion training.
